words: think of it more like end game is a breeding ranch… for a Pokémon champion with unlimited money, with unlimited land… and obviously with the power of Pokémon
think of this all written in the past tense… all of these Pokémon are retired and that's where this whole breeding ranch is like the centerpiece
I'm a breeder now, a retired champion, and the thing I do is tinker with different builds and trying to achieve different move sets and breeding stock that can go different ways
build a hatchery from scratch… interweave a hatchery and a greenhouse
It's all about the breeding stock. It's not really about the parent.
The compound should feel like a real place inhabited and operated by Pokémon, not a generic menu of buildings that passively generate points.
Think of it like the day care center gazillionaire edition… it's super exclusive, it's not massive, think more wildlife preserve with daycare aspect
It's other amazing trainers ... it costs so much money that you have to just have a ton of money.

rules.one_hq: One headquarters. Satellites only where the headquarters can't give a resident its land.
rules.access: Private ranch with one open feature: the Day-Care, a 'gazillionaire edition' of the games' Day-Care. Super exclusive and small, run like a wildlife preserve with a day-care side. Everything else is private.

residents.rule: Left open: any companion may retire to the ranch, stay with family, go back to the wild or go with the rival. Nobody is assigned; the census counts every companion as a possible resident.

stock.rule: Build the lineage, keep only the final product: one male of each target line who knows the whole egg-move set (the stud). The fathers used along the way are not kept. A line whose move comes from a held item keeps the item instead.

staffing.rule: Both Pokémon and people. Pokémon jobs come from game-backed or authored capabilities; people roles are placeholders to author.

glasshouse.name: The Glasshouse
glasshouse.idea: One building where eggs and plants share everything. Blackthorn sits against the Ice Path, so both need heat, and the heat comes from Pokémon. A Magcargo hearth at the core keeps the eggs warm; the greenhouse rings wrap around it and live on the same heat. Ampharos lights both through the winter. Eggs hatch by being walked, so the walk that hatches them runs through the crop rows: the egg walk is the harvest walk.

rooms.name: Glasshouse rings
rooms.what: berry beds and Apricorn trees wrapped around the hearth, warmed by it and lit by Ampharos in the dark months

rooms.name: Hatching loop
rooms.what: the walking path that winds through the glasshouse rows; eggs are carried around it until they hatch

rooms.name: Nursery yard

loop.note: proposed: one lap of the hatching loop = one Gen 4 egg cycle (255 steps), so an egg's cycle count is its lap count
loop.verify: 255 steps a cycle is believed (E-024); the spec asks to verify it before exact step counts

glasshouse.crops_note: The medicine crop for the clinic and the nursery, plus every berry your Pokémon's builds hold. Apricorns for Kurt's Poké Balls grow outside the glass (canon/ranch.json).

preserve.design: It doesn't take walk-ins: it's exclusive, small and by invitation. Clients' Pokémon don't sit in a pen. They live in real habitat on a protected piece of the land, cared for by keepers and by the ranch's own Pokémon. That's the preserve side; the day-care side is that their trainers come back for them. (RANCH.md §2, approved under D-040)
